spec.description: The Level II products that passed through one distribution host's LDM queue, oldest first from the start of the interval. JSON-LD: the products come as a `@graph`.

request.title: GetRadarQueueRequest
request.description: Which host, and which products. Every filter is optional.

limit.description: Most products to return, 1 to 50,000. Without it, 500.

arrived.description: Only products that arrived in this ISO 8601 interval: `start/end`, `start/duration` or `duration/end`, either end may be `NOW`, such as `2026-09-30T23:00:00Z/PT10M`. The answer starts at the interval's start, so a `limit` keeps the oldest. Without it, about the last two minutes. The service keeps about a week.

created.description: Only products the radar created in this ISO 8601 interval, in the same forms as `arrived`. Every request with it answered 503 on 2026-10-01 (`An upstream data source is temporarily unavailable`).

published.description: Only products published in this ISO 8601 interval, in the same forms as `arrived`.

station.description: Only this radar's products, such as `KATX`. An unknown one answers an empty `@graph`.

type.description: Only this kind of product. Undocumented; `start`, `intermediate`, `end` and `model` on 2026-10-01, which are the parts of a Level II volume.

feed.description: Only products from this feed, such as `NEXRAD2`.

resolution.description: Only products of this resolution version, such as `6` or `8`.

response.title: RadarQueue
response.description: The products, as a JSON-LD graph.

items.title: RadarQueueProduct
items.description: One Level II product in the queue.

arrivalTime.description: When the product arrived at the host.

type.description: Part of the Level II volume this is: `start`, `intermediate`, `end` or `model` on 2026-10-01. Undocumented, so not enumerated.

feed.description: Feed it came on, such as `NEXRAD2`.

sequenceNumber.description: Volume and chunk sequence, such as `490-050`.

size.description: Size of the product, in bytes.

notes: No `pagination` block. A walk would move the start of `arrived`, but `arrived` is one `start/end` string, not two parameters, and a `seek` block names its bounds as parameters. Products also share arrival times, so a walk keyed on them would need whole-row deduplication.

The documented `created` filter is in the request but has no example: every request with it answered 503 on 2026-10-01 (`An upstream data source is temporarily unavailable`), across four intervals and both hosts, and twice more later that day (`NOW/PT10M` on `rds`, `PT10M/NOW` on `tds`; correlationIds 8689f21 and 3f3fa5f7). The client sends it unchanged, so it works once the upstream source does.
The service keeps about a week (a window on 2026-09-20 answered an empty `@graph` on 2026-10-01), so `refresh_examples.py` moves the example's window to about a day ago before every re-recording.
